beats.text: A thief broke into a different house every night,
and every night, he stole exactly one thing.
One sock.
Not the pair. Just one.
No money missing. No jewelry touched.
Just a single, lonely sock, left behind in the drawer.
The newspapers called him the Sock Goblin.
The police just laughed.
A thief who steals one sock? That's not a crime. That's a laundry problem.
Months went by.
Ten houses.
Fifty.
Two hundred.
People started sleeping with their socks on.
Soon, nobody in town owned a matching pair.
Kids went to school in one red sock and one green one.
Then, a little shop opened on Market Street.
Fresh socks. Every pair guaranteed to match.
The line went around the block.
In one week, old Mr. Pickett sold a thousand pairs.
You see, a single sock is useless.
So the whole town had to buy new pairs.
But Mr. Pickett never knitted a single sock.
Every pair he sold was two stolen socks,
from two different houses.
A thousand pairs sold.
And not one of them was new.
